statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Current Tail risk remains in the low band.
recommendation: Current evidence indicates low Tail risk with elevated event and technology-sector stress; the U.S. cash open and 10:00 ET data window are the nearest defined checkpoints.
headline: Low Tail risk amid cautious stabilization before U.S. data
body: Tuesday's global session is subdued ahead of Nvidia earnings and U.S. data. U.S. equity futures are modestly firmer after Monday's technology-led decline, while Asian technology shares remain soft and Treasury yields have eased slightly. No verified persistent one-way NQ path is established at the assessment cutoff.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock-hours, Tail moved from low into WATCH during Monday's technology-led selloff, briefly reached elevated during the U.S. afternoon, then eased through WATCH and returned to low overnight. Stress fell sharply from extreme Monday levels; no published assessment was available for the immediately preceding 06:00 UTC slot.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours remain event-sensitive but do not imply a one-way path. Tail is projected to stay low through Europe, rise into WATCH around the U.S. cash open and 10:00 ET Consumer Confidence/New Home Sales window, then ease if post-release trade is two-way. Wednesday's GDP/PCE/durable-goods and Nvidia catalysts raise later event stress.

forecast.analysis: European cash-open liquidity can widen swings, but Tail stays low unless directional efficiency persists with shallow pullbacks and repeated extension.
Early European follow-through is the key test; two-way trade would keep mean-reversion conditions intact, while failed retracements would be adverse.
Mid-morning Europe remains mainly a structure checkpoint. Cross-asset alignment in yields, semiconductors and breadth would matter more than move size alone.
Approaching U.S. premarket liquidity, event anticipation raises Stress modestly; Tail remains low without a persistent directional NQ path.
U.S. premarket participation can amplify Monday's technology weakness or reverse it. Repeated extension after shallow pullbacks is the conditional Tail trigger.
The U.S. cash-open approach lifts Tail to WATCH conditionally. A gap-and-go with aligned semiconductors and yields would be more concerning than ordinary opening volatility.
The cash open and the 10:00 ET data window form the peak near-term risk cluster. WATCH reflects conditional whipsaw or continuation risk, not an already-observed no-retracement path.
After the scheduled Consumer Confidence and New Home Sales releases, Tail remains WATCH unless price discovery is two-way; sustained extension after failed retracements is the adverse path.
Tail can return to low if post-release price discovery is two-way and volatility decays; persistent extension would invalidate that easing path.
Late-morning U.S. trade should clarify whether the opening move is durable. Balanced retracements favor low Tail; session-extreme holding would keep risk firmer.
Midday liquidity usually reduces directional urgency, though technology-sector concentration can still create sharp moves. Tail remains low absent renewed extension.
Early U.S. afternoon is modeled as normal conditional structure if the data impulse has been absorbed and cross-assets are not reinforcing a one-way move.
Afternoon consolidation would keep Tail low. A fresh catalyst-driven break with shallow pullbacks would be the principal adverse deviation.
Later U.S. afternoon remains low Tail under two-way trade; semiconductors and megacaps are the main confirmation channels for any renewed Nasdaq impulse.
Approaching power hour, Stress is moderate while Tail stays low unless price reclaims a session extreme and holds it with broad technology confirmation.
Power-hour risk is conditional rather than automatic. Repeated extension with weak retracement quality would lift Tail; ordinary closing flows would not.
Into the cash close, Tail remains low if closing flows stay balanced. A one-way closing auction would be the main structure checkpoint.
Immediately after the cash close, liquidity thins and single-stock headlines can matter more. Tail stays low absent a verified index-level continuation mechanism.
Early after-hours trade is modeled as mixed, with attention shifting toward Wednesday's major macro and Nvidia catalysts outside this hour.
Evening U.S. liquidity is thin; isolated moves carry less Tail significance unless they persist across futures and aligned cross-assets.
Overnight transition risk is modestly higher as markets begin positioning for Wednesday's GDP/PCE and durable-goods releases, but those events remain future checkpoints.
Early Asia hours may reflect positioning for Wednesday catalysts. Tail remains low unless a persistent directional futures path develops with poor retracement quality.
Later Asia trade carries rising event anticipation ahead of Wednesday's U.S. macro cluster; Stress increases, while Tail remains below WATCH absent observed one-way structure.
